hook.convey: one whole (a roti, a drawn circle) cut and shared → fair only if the pieces are the same size; equal pieces of one whole get the names half, third, quarter; the number of pieces alone does not decide the name

use.hi: Socho, Maa ne kitchen mein ek garam roti banayi, aur tum do bhai-behen ho. Roti ke 2 tukde honge. Dono ke tukde sach mein barabar kab hote hain, aaj wahi pakadna hai.
use.en: Picture it: Mum just made a hot roti in the kitchen, and there are two of you. The roti becomes 2 pieces. Today we catch exactly when both pieces are really equal.

use.hi: Drawing book kholo aur ek gol circle banao. Usko barabar tukdon mein baantenge, phir ek tukda colour karenge. Us rangin tukde ka bhi ek naam hota hai, woh dhoondhenge.
use.en: Open your drawing book and draw a round circle. We'll split it into equal pieces and colour one piece. That coloured piece has a name too, and we'll find it.

explain.convey: roti cut into 2 same-size pieces → each piece = half = 1/2; bottom 2 = equal pieces in the whole, top 1 = pieces taken

point.hi: Yeh roti dekho. 2 barabar tukde, aur ek tukde mein rang hai. Woh tukda roti ka aadha hai, likhte hain 1/2. Neeche ka 2, roti ke kul barabar tukde. Upar ka 1, jitne tukde humne liye.
point.en: Look at this roti. 2 equal pieces, and one piece is coloured. That piece is half the roti, and we write it 1/2. The 2 at the bottom: all the roti's equal pieces. The 1 on top: the pieces we took.

pointAlt.hi: Socho, tum aur ek dost ek roti baant rahe ho, aur dono ko bilkul ek jitna mila. Tumhara tukda poori roti ka aadha hai. Roti kitne barabar tukdon mein bati, woh ginti neeche likhte hain, aur tumhare paas kitne tukde hain, woh upar.
pointAlt.en: Think of you and a friend sharing a roti, each getting exactly the same. Your piece is half of the whole roti. How many equal pieces the roti was shared into is written at the bottom, and how many pieces you have goes on top.

prompt.hi: Ek tukda rangin hai, ek bina rang ka. Toh kya rangin tukda 1/1 hua, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: One piece is coloured, one is not. So is the coloured piece 1/1, yes or no?

why.hi: rangin tukda roti ke 2 barabar tukdon mein se 1 hai, toh neeche 2 aata hai, 1 nahi
why.en: the coloured piece is 1 of the roti's 2 equal pieces, so 2 goes at the bottom, not 1

whyAlt.hi: 1/1 ka matlab hota poori roti, par rangin tukda toh roti ka sirf ek aadha hai
whyAlt.en: 1/1 would mean the whole roti, but the coloured piece is only one half of it

simpler.hi: Neeche wala number saare tukde ginta hai, rangin bhi aur saade bhi, yahan kul 2. Upar sirf rangin wale.
simpler.en: The bottom number counts every piece, coloured and plain, here 2 in all. The top counts only the coloured ones.

explain.convey: a pizza and a cake, 3 pieces each, but only same-size pieces get the name third: the cake's equal pieces are each 1/3; the pizza has one big and two small pieces → asked: is a small one a third

point.hi: Yeh pizza aur yeh cake, dono ke 3-3 tukde. Cake ke teeno tukde barabar hain, toh wahan har tukda ek-tihaai hai, 1/3. Pizza mein ek tukda bada hai aur do chhote.
point.en: Here's a pizza and a cake, 3 pieces each. The cake's three pieces are equal, so there each piece is one-third, 1/3. The pizza has one big piece and two small ones.

pointAlt.hi: Teen dost ek cake baantein aur har dost ko bilkul ek jaisa tukda mile, tab har tukda cake ka ek-tihaai kehlata hai. Pizza ke bhi 3 tukde hain, par woh ek size ke nahi: ek bada, do chhote.
pointAlt.en: When three friends share a cake and each gets exactly the same piece, each piece is called one-third of the cake. The pizza has 3 pieces too, but they are not one size: one big, two small.

prompt.hi: Pizza ka ek chhota tukda lo. Kya woh pizza ka ek-tihaai hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Take a small piece of the pizza. Is it one-third of the pizza, yes or no?

reask.hi: Kya pizza ka ek chhota tukda poore pizza ka ek-tihaai hai?
reask.en: Is a small piece of the pizza one-third of the whole pizza?

accept: no, the pieces are not equal

why.hi: pizza ke tukde chhote-bade hain, aur ek-tihaai tabhi banta hai jab 3 tukde barabar hon
why.en: the pizza's pieces are big and small, and a third needs 3 equal pieces

whyAlt.hi: chhota tukda ek-tihaai hota toh teen chhote tukde milkar poora pizza bana dete, par yahan ek tukda bada hai
whyAlt.en: if a small piece were a third, three small pieces would make the whole pizza, but here one piece is big

simpler.hi: Ek chhota tukda bade tukde ke paas rakho, dono ek size ke nahi. Aise tukdon ko ek-tihaai nahi kehte.
simpler.en: Put a small piece beside the big one, and they are not the same size. Pieces like that are not called thirds.

explain.convey: drawn circle in 3 equal parts → one part = one-third = 1/3; bottom 3 = all the equal parts of the whole

point.hi: Is circle ke 3 barabar tukde hain, ek mein rang. Yeh rangin tukda ek-tihaai hai, 1/3. Neeche 3 isliye, kyunki poore circle ke 3 barabar tukde hain.
point.en: This circle has 3 equal pieces, one coloured. That coloured piece is one-third, 1/3. The 3 goes at the bottom because the whole circle has 3 equal pieces.

pointAlt.hi: Ek circle ko 3 dost barabar baantein, toh har dost ko circle ka ek-tihaai milta hai. Board par jo ek rangin tukda hai, woh ek dost ka tukda hai, 1/3. Neeche ka 3 batata hai ki circle kitne barabar tukdon mein bata.
pointAlt.en: If 3 friends share a circle equally, each friend gets one-third of the circle. The one coloured piece on the board is one friend's piece, 1/3. The 3 at the bottom tells how many equal pieces the circle was shared into.

prompt.hi: Ek aur tukda rang do. Ab circle ka kitna bhaag rangin hai, fraction mein?
prompt.en: Colour one more piece. Now what fraction of the circle is coloured?

reask.hi: Circle ke 3 barabar tukdon mein se 2 mein rang ho, toh circle ka kitna bhaag rangin hai?
reask.en: If 2 of the circle's 3 equal pieces are coloured, what fraction of the circle is coloured?

why.hi: circle 3 barabar tukdon mein bata hai aur ab 2 mein rang hai, yaani 2/3
why.en: the circle has 3 equal pieces and 2 are coloured now, so 2/3

whyAlt.hi: sirf ek tukda bina rang ka bacha, toh rangin bhaag poore circle se ek-tihaai kam hai: 2/3
whyAlt.en: only one piece is left plain, so the coloured part is one-third short of the whole circle: 2/3

simpler.hi: Circle wahi hai, toh neeche 3 hi rahega. Bas upar ki ginti badlegi: jitne tukdon mein rang, utna upar.
simpler.en: It is the same circle, so 3 stays at the bottom. Only the top changes: as many pieces as are coloured.

explain.convey: strip in 8 equal parts, 1 shaded → one-eighth = 1/8; bottom = all 8 parts of the whole, never the 7 unshaded parts left → not 1/7; then asked on a second strip (a bar of 6 equal pieces, 1 eaten, 5 left) → 1/6, not 1/5

point.hi: Is baar upar wali patti ke 8 barabar tukde hain. Ek mein rang, saat khaali. Rangin tukda 1/8 hai. Dhyaan do, neeche 8 aata hai, saare tukde. Bache hue 7 nahi.
point.en: This time the top strip has 8 equal pieces. One coloured, seven empty. The coloured piece is 1/8. Notice: 8 goes at the bottom, all the pieces. Not the 7 left over.

pointAlt.hi: Rangin tukde jaise 8 tukde ek ke baad ek rakho, toh poori upar wali patti ban jaati hai; isliye har tukda 1/8 hai. Ek tukda kha bhi lo, patti toh 8 tukdon se hi bani thi, isliye neeche 8 hi rehta hai.
pointAlt.en: Lay 8 pieces like the coloured one end to end and you get the whole top strip; that is why each piece is 1/8. Even if one piece is eaten, the strip was still made of 8 pieces, so 8 stays at the bottom.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali patti ek chocolate bar hai, 6 barabar tukde. 1 tukda kha liya, 5 bache. Bar ka kitna bhaag khaya gaya, fraction mein?
prompt.en: The bottom strip is a chocolate bar, 6 equal pieces. 1 piece got eaten, 5 are left. How much of the bar got eaten, as a fraction?

reask.hi: 6 barabar tukdon wali chocolate bar ka ek tukda khaya gaya, toh bar ka kitna bhaag khaya gaya?
reask.en: 1 piece of a chocolate bar of 6 equal pieces was eaten: what fraction of the bar was eaten?

why.hi: upar ka rangin tukda 1/8 hai; waise bar ke 6 mein se 1 tukda khaya, toh 1/6; bache 5 neeche nahi jaate
why.en: the top coloured piece is 1/8; likewise 1 of 6 bar pieces was eaten, so 1/6; the 5 left never go below

whyAlt.hi: khaane se pehle bar ke 6 tukde the; khaya hua tukda un 6 mein se ek hai, isliye 1/6, chahe kitne bhi bache hon
whyAlt.en: before anyone ate, the bar had 6 pieces; the eaten piece is one of those 6, so 1/6, however many are left

simpler.hi: Pehle poori patti socho, khaane se pehle. Tab jitne tukde the, wahi neeche jaate hain; bache hue nahi.
simpler.en: First picture the whole strip, before anyone ate. However many pieces it had, that goes at the bottom; not the ones left.

problem.hi: Ek lambi barfi ke 5 barabar tukde kiye, aur 3 tukde kha liye. Barfi ka kitna bhaag khaya gaya?
problem.en: A long barfi is cut into 5 equal pieces, and 3 pieces get eaten. What fraction of the barfi was eaten?

problemAlt.hi: Socho, barfi ki ek lambi patti ke 5 barabar tukde kaate gaye. Shaam tak plate par sirf 2 tukde bache, baaki sab kha liye gaye. Ab nikalna hai ki khaye hue tukde poori barfi ka kitna bhaag hain.
problemAlt.en: Picture a long strip of barfi cut into 5 equal pieces. By evening only 2 pieces are left on the plate; all the rest were eaten. Now we find what part of the whole barfi the eaten pieces are.

simpler.hi: Ek barfi ke 5 barabar tukde hain, aur unmein se 3 kha liye. Socho, kitne mein se kitne khaye gaye.
simpler.en: One barfi is in 5 equal pieces, and 3 of them were eaten. Think how many out of how many were eaten.

givens.hi: Hamare paas do cheezein hain: poori barfi ke tukde, aur khaye hue tukde.
givens.en: We know two things: the pieces of the whole barfi, and the pieces eaten.

find.en: the eaten part, as a fraction

why.hi: woh poori barfi ke saare barabar tukde ginta hai
why.en: it counts all the equal pieces of the whole barfi

simpler.hi: Barfi kaatne ke baad, khaane se pehle, kitne tukde the, woh gino. Wahi ginti neeche jaati hai, yahan 5.
simpler.en: Count the pieces right after cutting, before anyone eats. That count goes at the bottom, here 5.

why.hi: woh sirf khaye hue tukde ginta hai
why.en: it counts only the pieces that were eaten

simpler.hi: Ab sirf khaye hue tukde gino, bache hue chhod do. Woh 3 hain, toh upar 3.
simpler.en: Now count only the eaten pieces and skip the rest. That's 3, so 3 on top.

prompt.hi: Dono numbers ko ek saath likho, beech mein line. Toh khaya hua bhaag kitna hai?
prompt.en: Write the two numbers together with a line between them. So what is the eaten part?

reask.hi: Barfi ke 5 barabar tukdon mein se 3 khaye gaye, toh barfi ka kitna bhaag khaya gaya?
reask.en: 3 of the barfi's 5 equal pieces were eaten: what fraction of the barfi was eaten?

why.hi: 5 barabar tukdon mein se 3 khaye gaye, isliye neeche 5 aur upar 3 aata hai
why.en: 3 of the 5 equal pieces were eaten, so 5 goes below and 3 on top

whyAlt.hi: bache hue do tukde barfi ka 2/5 hain, aur khaye hue baaki 3, yaani 3/5; dono milkar 5/5, poori barfi
whyAlt.en: the 2 pieces left are 2/5 of the barfi and the eaten ones the other 3, so 3/5; together 5/5, the whole barfi

simpler.hi: Humne dekha, neeche 5 aata hai aur upar 3. Bas dono ko ek fraction mein likh do.
simpler.en: We saw that 5 goes below and 3 on top. Just put them into one fraction.

why.hi: 5 barabar tukdon mein se 3 khaye gaye; bache hue 2 tukde neeche nahi jaate
why.en: 3 of the 5 equal pieces were eaten; the 2 pieces left over do not go at the bottom

prompt.hi: Laddoo toota aur 3 tukde ho gaye, ek bada aur do chhote. Board par dekho: bada tukda laddoo ka kitna bhaag hai?
prompt.en: A laddoo broke into 3 pieces, one big and two small. Look at the board: what fraction of the laddoo is the big piece?

why.hi: laddoo ke 3 tukdon mein bada tukda theek aadha hai, yaani 1/2; dono chhote milkar baaki aadha
why.en: of the laddoo's 3 pieces, the big one is exactly half, 1/2; the two small ones make the other half

whyAlt.hi: teen tukde hain par barabar nahi, isliye 1/3 nahi; bada tukda laddoo ka theek aadha gherta hai, 1/2
whyAlt.en: there are three pieces but not equal ones, so not 1/3; the big piece covers exactly half the laddoo, 1/2

simpler.hi: Dono chhote tukde jodo aur bade tukde se milao. Dono taraf barabar ho, toh bada tukda aadha hai.
simpler.en: Put the two small pieces together and match them with the big one. If both sides are equal, the big piece is a half.

prompt.hi: Tumhari chocolate ke 5 barabar tukde hue, aur tumne 1 kha liya. Bache hue tukde poori chocolate ka kitna bhaag hain, fraction mein?
prompt.en: Your chocolate splits into 5 equal pieces, and you eat 1. What fraction of the whole chocolate are the pieces left?

reask.hi: 5 barabar tukdon wali chocolate ka ek tukda khaya gaya, toh bache hue tukde chocolate ka kitna bhaag hain?
reask.en: 1 piece of a chocolate of 5 equal pieces was eaten: what fraction of the chocolate are the pieces left?

why.hi: chocolate ke 5 barabar tukdon mein se 4 bache, yaani 4/5; neeche poori chocolate ke saare 5 tukde aate hain
why.en: 4 of the chocolate's 5 equal pieces are left, so 4/5; all 5 pieces of the whole chocolate go at the bottom

whyAlt.hi: khaya hua ek tukda 1/5 hai aur poori chocolate 5/5; 5 mein se ek gaya, toh 4/5 bacha
whyAlt.en: the 1 eaten piece is 1/5 and the whole chocolate is 5/5; 1 of 5 went, so 4/5 is left

simpler.hi: Poori chocolate ke saare tukde neeche, aur jo bache woh upar. Khaya hua tukda upar nahi gina jaata.
simpler.en: All the chocolate's pieces at the bottom, and the ones left on top. The eaten piece is not counted on top.

prompt.hi: Cake ke 4 tukde hue: 1 bada aur 3 chhote. {friend} ka kehna hai ki ek chhota tukda cake ke 1/4 se bhi chhota hai. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: A cake is cut into 4 pieces: 1 big and 3 small. {friend} says one small piece is even smaller than 1/4 of the cake. Is that right?

reask.hi: Cake ke ek bade aur 3 chhote tukdon mein, kya ek chhota tukda cake ke 1/4 se chhota hai?
reask.en: With a cake in 1 big and 3 small pieces, is one small piece smaller than 1/4 of the cake?

why.hi: bada tukda aadha cake hai; teeno chhote milkar baaki aadha, toh har chhota tukda 1/4 se chhota hai
why.en: the big piece is half; the three small ones together make the other half, so each is less than 1/4

whyAlt.hi: charon tukde barabar hote toh har ek 1/4 hota; yahan bada tukda zyada le gaya, toh chhote tukde 1/4 se chhote reh gaye
whyAlt.en: if all four pieces were equal each would be 1/4; here the big piece took more, so the small ones are left smaller than 1/4

simpler.hi: Teeno chhote tukde milkar bade tukde jitne hain, yaani aadha cake. Aur 1/4 toh aadhe ka bhi aadha hota hai.
simpler.en: The three small pieces together match the big one: half the cake. And 1/4 is half of a half.

ladder.why: more than one part taken → 3 of 4 equal parts = 3/4; top number beyond 1
error spot: parts left used as bottom → bottom = whole's equal parts
harder contrast with quarters on flags → equality decides, count alone does not

remediation.move: fair-sharing story, imagined: a rope cut into 1 long piece + some short ones → not a fair split → counting the pieces does not name them as fractions; then a sheet of paper folded down the middle and cut into 2 same-size pieces → only then is each piece a half → first check the pieces are the same size; then the torn roti on the board, asked as a direct claim (is the bigger piece more than half?)

say.hi: Ek rassi socho, jo ek lambe aur kuch chhote tukdon mein kati. Yeh baant barabar nahi, isliye tukde gin kar fraction naam nahi rakh sakte. Ab ek kaagaz ko theek beech se modo aur kaato: dono tukde ek jaise hain, tabhi har tukda aadha hai.
say.en: Picture a rope cut into one long piece and a few short ones. That split is unfair, so counting pieces cannot name them as fractions. Now fold a paper exactly in half and cut it: both pieces match, and only then is each a half.

simpler.hi: Chhote-bade tukde gin kar naam nahi rakhte; pehle dekho, tukde ek size ke hain ya nahi, jaise kaagaz ke do aadhe.
simpler.en: You can't name big-and-small pieces by counting them; first check whether the pieces are the same size, like the paper's two halves.

prompt.hi: Roti ke 2 tukde hue: ek bada, ek chhota. Kya bada tukda roti ke aadhe se zyada hai?
prompt.en: A roti tears into 2 pieces, one bigger, one smaller. Is the bigger piece more than half the roti?

accept: yes, it is more than half

why.hi: do tukde barabar hon tabhi har ek aadha hota; yahan bada tukda chhote se bada hai, toh aadhe se zyada
why.en: two pieces are halves only when equal; here the bigger one is more than the smaller, so it is more than half

whyAlt.hi: aadha tab hota jab dono tukde ek jitne hote; bada tukda chhote se zyada roti le gaya, isliye woh aadhe se aage nikal gaya
whyAlt.en: it would be a half only if both pieces were the same; the bigger piece took more roti than the smaller, so it goes past the half

simpler.hi: Socho, do barabar tukde hote toh har ek aadha hota. Yahan ek tukda doosre se bada hai.
simpler.en: Think: with two equal pieces, each would be a half. Here one piece is bigger than the other.

remediation.move: name the piece first: each piece of a whole of equal pieces is named by how many such pieces make the whole, eaten or left → the bottom number names the piece, the top only counts how many such pieces were taken; pieces left never rename it; then the then-card's own bar of 4 pieces with 2 coloured (eaten): which number goes at the bottom

say.hi: Jab chocolate bar ke saare tukde barabar hon, tukde ka naam is se aata hai ki poori bar aise kitne tukdon se bani hai. Khaya ho ya bacha, naam wahi. Neeche ka number tukde ka naam hai; upar bas ginti, kitne tukde liye.
say.en: When all the pieces of a chocolate bar are equal, a piece is named by how many such pieces make the whole bar. Eaten or left, the name stays. The bottom number names the piece; the top just counts how many were taken.

simpler.hi: Neeche ka number poori bar ke saare tukde ginta hai, khaye hue bhi aur bache hue bhi. Upar sirf woh tukde aate hain jinki baat poochhi gayi hai.
simpler.en: The bottom number counts all the bar's pieces, eaten and left. The top counts only the pieces the question asks about.

prompt.hi: Is chocolate bar ke rangin tukde kha liye gaye. Khaye hue bhaag ka fraction likhna ho, toh neeche kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The coloured pieces of this bar were eaten. To write the eaten part as a fraction, which number goes at the bottom?

reask.hi: Board ki chocolate bar ke rangin tukde khaye gaye, toh khaye hue bhaag ke fraction mein neeche kaunsa number aayega?
reask.en: The coloured pieces of the bar on the board were eaten: which number goes at the bottom of the eaten part's fraction?

why.hi: neeche poori bar ke saare barabar tukde aate hain, yahan 4; khaya hua bhaag 2/4 hai, bache hue 2 neeche nahi jaate
why.en: all the bar's equal pieces go at the bottom, here 4; the eaten part is 2/4; the 2 left never go there

whyAlt.hi: agar bache hue 2 neeche likhte toh 2/2 ban jaata, yaani poori bar, par poori bar toh khayi nahi gayi; isliye neeche saare 4 tukde aate hain
whyAlt.en: if the 2 left went at the bottom it would be 2/2, the whole bar, but the whole bar was not eaten; so all 4 pieces go at the bottom

simpler.hi: Khaane se pehle bar mein kitne tukde the, board par sab gino, rangin bhi aur saade bhi.
simpler.en: Count how many pieces the bar had before anyone ate: all of them on the board, coloured and plain.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab ek cheez nahi, bahut saare laddoo lenge, aur unke barabar group banayenge. Niyam wahi rahega: sab barabar.
bridgeToNext.en: Next we take lots of laddoos, not one thing, and make equal groups. The rule stays the same: everything equal.

simpler.hi: Ab bahut saare laddoo ke barabar group banayenge.
simpler.en: Now we make equal groups of lots of laddoos.

hook.convey: 12 laddoos (or 12 biscuits), 2 sharers, fair share → each share = half of the set; a fraction can be of a whole set, the set being the one whole

use.hi: Kitchen ke dibbe mein 12 laddoo rakhe hain, aur khaane wale tum do. Kisi ko kam nahi milna chahiye. 12 laddoo ka aadha kitna hota hai, aaj yahi nikalenge.
use.en: There are 12 laddoos in the kitchen tin, and two of you to eat them. Nobody should get fewer. Today we work out what half of 12 laddoos is.

use.hi: Cricket match ke baad 2 bhookhe bachche ghar aaye, aur dibbe mein 12 laddoo hain. Dono ko ek jitne laddoo dene hain, warna jhagda hoga. Ek bachche ko 12 ka aadha milega.
use.en: After a cricket match 2 hungry children come home, and there are 12 laddoos in the tin. Both must get the same number, or there'll be a fight. Each child gets half of the 12.

explain.convey: the tin's 12 laddoos, shown in 4 equal groups of 3 → half = 2 equal shares, so each of the two gets 2 of the groups; one share's count is the half; check: both shares together make all 12 again

point.hi: Yeh 12 laddoo hain, aur do bachche inhe barabar baantenge. Board par inke 4 barabar group bane, har group mein 3. Aadha matlab dono ko ek jitna, toh har bachche ko 2 group milenge. Jaanch bhi aasaan hai: dono bachchon ke laddoo jodo, toh 12 wapas.
point.en: Here are 12 laddoos, and two children will share them equally. On the board they're in 4 equal groups, 3 in each group. Half means both get the same, so each child gets 2 groups. Checking is easy too: put both children's laddoos together and all 12 are back.

pointAlt.hi: Aadha karne ka ek aur tareeka: laddoo ek-ek karke do plate mein baari-baari rakho, jab tak sab khatam na ho jaayein. Dono plate mein ek jitne laddoo aayenge, aur ek plate ke laddoo hi aadha hain.

prompt.hi: Do bachche yeh 12 laddoo barabar baant lete hain. 12 laddoo ka aadha kitne laddoo hai?

why.hi: 12 laddoo 2 barabar group mein jaayein toh har group mein 6, aur 2 × 6 = 12
why.en: 12 laddoos in 2 equal groups puts 6 in each, and 2 × 6 = 12

whyAlt.hi: laddoo ek-ek karke do plate mein rakho toh har plate mein 6 aate hain; 6 aur 6 milkar 12
whyAlt.en: put the laddoos one at a time onto two plates and each plate gets 6; 6 and 6 make 12

explain.convey: 24 mangoes shown as 1/6 (6 equal groups of 4): bottom 6 = share into 6 equal groups, top 1 = take one group; then 1/3 of the same 24: bottom 3 = 3 equal groups, one group's count is the answer

point.hi: Ab yeh 24 aam dekho, 6 barabar group mein, har group mein 4. 1/6 ka neeche wala 6 kehta hai: 6 barabar group banao. Upar ka 1 kehta hai: ek group lo. Toh 24 ka 1/6 hai 4 aam. 1/3 mein bhi yahi hota hai, bas neeche wala 3 hai.
point.en: Now look at these 24 mangoes, in 6 equal groups, 4 in each group. The 6 at the bottom of 1/6 says: make 6 equal groups. The 1 on top says: take one group. So 1/6 of 24 is 4 mangoes. 1/3 works the same way, only the 3 at the bottom is different.

pointAlt.hi: Ulta socho: 6 bachche yeh 24 aam barabar baantein, toh har bachche ko ek group milta hai, 4 aam, aur yahi 24 ka 1/6 hai. Bachche kam hon, jaise 3, toh har bachche ke paas zyada aam aayenge.
pointAlt.en: Think of it the other way: if 6 children share these 24 mangoes equally, each child gets one group, 4 mangoes, and that is 1/6 of 24. With fewer children, say 3, each child would get more mangoes.

simpler.hi: 3 ka pahada yaad karo. 3 ko kis number se guna karein ki 24 bane, wahi ek group hai.

pointAlt.hi: Kisi cheez ka fraction nikalna ho, toh neeche ka number batata hai kitne bachche barabar baant rahe hain. Yahan 2 bachche yeh 20 kanche baant rahe hain: har bachche ko 10, yaani 20 ka aadha 10.
pointAlt.en: To find a fraction of some things, the bottom number tells how many children share them equally. Here 2 children share these 20 marbles: each child gets 10, so half of 20 is 10.

simpler.hi: Upar wali patti ka ek tukda dekho, aur uske theek neeche wale chhote tukde ek-ek karke gino.
simpler.en: Look at one piece of the top strip, and count the small pieces right under it one by one.

answer.hi: 1/3 wala tukda bada hai, aur us par 1/6 wale 2 tukde aate hain
answer.en: the 1/3 piece is bigger, and 2 of the 1/6 pieces fit on it

why.hi: wahi bar 6 mein kati toh 3 wala har tukda do mein bat gaya; 6 bada number hai, par 1/6 chhota tukda
why.en: cut into 6, each third splits in two; 6 is the bigger number, but 1/6 is the smaller piece

prompt.hi: Meena ek roti 2 barabar tukdon mein kaatti hai. Sonu waisi hi roti 9 barabar tukdon mein kaatta hai. Dono apna ek-ek tukda lete hain. Kiska tukda roti ke 1/3 se chhota hai, Meena ka ya Sonu ka?
prompt.en: Meena cuts a roti into 2 equal pieces. Sonu cuts the same kind of roti into 9 equal pieces. Each takes one piece. Whose piece is smaller than 1/3 of the roti, Meena's or Sonu's?

why.hi: Meena ka tukda 1/2, jo 1/3 se bada; Sonu ki roti 9 tukdon mein kati, toh uska 1/9 tukda 1/3 se chhota
why.en: Meena's piece is 1/2, bigger than 1/3; Sonu's roti is in 9 pieces, so his 1/9 is smaller than 1/3

whyAlt.hi: 1/3 matlab roti ke 3 barabar tukde; Meena ki roti 3 se kam tukdon mein kati toh uska tukda bada, Sonu ki 3 se zyada tukdon mein kati toh uska tukda chhota
whyAlt.en: 1/3 means a roti in 3 equal pieces; Meena's roti is in fewer than 3 pieces, so her piece is bigger, Sonu's in more than 3, so his piece is smaller

simpler.hi: Jo roti jitne zyada tukdon mein kati, uske tukde utne patle. 2 tukde aur 9 tukde, dono ko 1/3 wale tukde se milao.
simpler.en: The more pieces a roti is cut into, the thinner each piece. Compare 2 pieces and 9 pieces with a 1/3 piece.

prompt.hi: Ek chocolate bar 8 bachchon mein barabar bati, aur utni hi badi doosri bar 2 bachchon mein. Farhan 8 waalon mein hai, Gita 2 waalon mein. Farhan kehta hai use zyada mila, kyunki 8 bada hai. Kise zyada mila, Farhan ko ya Gita ko?
prompt.en: One chocolate bar is shared equally by 8 children, and a bar the same size by 2. Farhan is with the 8, Gita with the 2. Farhan says he got more, because 8 is bigger. Who got more, Farhan or Gita?

reask.hi: Ek bar 8 bachchon mein bati jinmein Farhan hai, aur waisi hi bar 2 bachchon mein jinmein Gita hai, toh kise zyada mila, Farhan ko ya Gita ko?
reask.en: One bar is shared by 8 children, Farhan among them, and a bar just like it by 2, Gita among them: who got more, Farhan or Gita?

why.hi: 8 mein bati bar ka har tukda 1/8 hai, 2 mein bati ka 1/2; 1/2 bada hai, toh Gita ko zyada mila
why.en: shared by 8, each piece is 1/8; shared by 2, it is 1/2; 1/2 is bigger, so Gita got more

whyAlt.hi: Gita ki bar sirf 2 bachchon mein bati, toh use aadhi bar mili; Farhan ko 8 mein se ek patla tukda mila
whyAlt.en: Gita's bar was shared by only 2 children, so she got half a bar; Farhan got one thin piece out of 8

simpler.hi: Ek hi bar ko jitne zyada bachche baantein, har bachche ka tukda utna patla. Farhan ki taraf 8 bachche hain.
simpler.en: The more children share the same bar, the thinner each piece. Farhan's side has 8 children.

prompt.hi: Ek hi chocolate bar ke teen tukde: 1/4, 1/10 aur 1/7. Inhe sabse chhote se sabse bade tak lagao.
prompt.en: Three pieces of the same chocolate bar: 1/4, 1/10 and 1/7. Put them in order from smallest to biggest.

reask.hi: Ek hi bar ke 1/4, 1/10 aur 1/7 tukdon ko sabse chhote se sabse bade tak kaise lagaoge?
reask.en: How do you put 1/4, 1/10 and 1/7 pieces of one bar in order, smallest to biggest?

why.hi: bar jitne zyada tukdon mein kate, tukda utna chhota; isliye pehle 1/10, phir 1/7, phir 1/4
why.en: the more pieces a bar is cut into, the smaller the piece, so 1/10 first, then 1/7, then 1/4

whyAlt.hi: socho 10 dost, 7 dost aur 4 dost ek-ek bar baant rahe hain; 10 dost waalon ka tukda sabse chhota, 4 dost waalon ka sabse bada
whyAlt.en: picture 10 friends, 7 friends and 4 friends each sharing a bar; the 10 friends get the smallest piece, the 4 friends the biggest

simpler.hi: Sabse chhota tukda woh, jiski bar sabse zyada tukdon mein kati. Wahan se shuru karo.
simpler.en: The smallest piece comes from the bar cut into the most pieces. Start there.

ladder.why: say why 1/2 beats 1/4 when 4 > 2 → the rule in words, a frame no card asks
1/5 vs 1/8 of one roti as a quick compare → the rule on two new denominators, after the lesson used 6, 4, 2, 9
link back to collections → 1/3 and 1/4 of 12 slices as amounts, then the difference

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (two same cakes, 9 and 7 equal pieces), naming none of its numbers: a bigger bottom number does not mean a bigger piece; it says how many equal pieces the whole was cut into, and more equal pieces of the same whole → thinner pieces → then the child judges the cakes as a direct claim (is a piece of the 7-piece cake bigger than a piece of the 9-piece cake?)

say.hi: Yeh dono cake ek jitne bade hain. Bada number matlab bada tukda nahi: neeche ka number batata hai ki cake kitne barabar tukdon mein kata. Jitne zyada barabar tukde, utna patla har tukda.
say.en: These two cakes are the same size. A bigger number is not a bigger piece: the bottom number tells how many equal pieces the cake was cut into. The more equal pieces, the thinner each piece.

simpler.hi: Socho, ek hi cake pehle kam tukdon mein kata, phir zyada mein. Cake utna hi rehta hai, toh zyada tukde matlab patle tukde.
simpler.en: Think of one cake cut first into a few pieces, then into many. The cake stays the same size, so more pieces means thinner pieces.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake: ek ke 9 barabar tukde, ek ke 7. Kya 7 tukdon wale cake ka tukda, 9 tukdon wale ke tukde se bada hai?
prompt.en: Two same cakes: one in 9 equal pieces, one in 7. Is a piece of the 7-piece cake bigger than a piece of the 9-piece cake?

accept: haan, 7 wale ka tukda bada hai
yes, the 7-piece cake's piece is bigger

why.hi: 7 tukdon wala cake kam barabar tukdon mein kata, toh uska har tukda 9 wale se bada hai
why.en: the 7-piece cake is cut into fewer equal pieces, so each piece is bigger than the 9-piece cake's

whyAlt.hi: 9 log aur 7 log ek jaise cake baantein, toh 7 waalon mein har ek ko bada tukda milega, kyunki log kam hain
whyAlt.en: if 9 people and 7 people share cakes just alike, each of the 7 gets a bigger piece, because there are fewer people

simpler.hi: 9 aur 7 batate hain cake kitne barabar tukdon mein kata; zyada tukde, chhote tukde.
simpler.en: 9 and 7 say how many equal pieces each cake was cut into; more pieces, smaller pieces.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke 9 barabar tukde hain, aur 4 tukdon mein rang hai. Rangin bhaag fraction mein kitna hai?
prompt.en: This circle has 9 equal pieces, and 4 pieces are coloured. What fraction is the coloured part?

why.hi: circle ke saare 9 barabar tukde neeche aate hain aur rangin 4 upar; bina rang ke 5 neeche nahi jaate
why.en: all 9 equal pieces of the circle go at the bottom and the 4 coloured ones on top; the 5 plain ones never go at the bottom

covered.hi: Aaj ki baat yeh thi ki tukde barabar hon tabhi unka fraction naam banta hai, aur neeche ka number poori cheez ke saare barabar tukde ginta hai. Phir cheezon ke group ka fraction aaya, aur yeh ki ek hi cheez jitne zyada tukdon mein kate, har tukda utna chhota hota hai.
covered.en: Today was about how pieces get a fraction name only when they are equal, and how the bottom number counts all the equal pieces of the whole. Then came fractions of a group of things, and how the more pieces one same thing is cut into, the smaller each piece is.

goodbye.hi: Aaj ke liye itna hi, phir milte hain!
goodbye.en: That's all for today, see you next time!
